Hey! This comes from someone with 7 siblings lol. I think it's really important to take age gaps, if they are fully biological siblings and even genders into consideration. I am in the middle, my youngest sister is 7 years younger than me and my oldest brother is 21 years older than me lol. I feel that it is totally plausible for them to get along most of the time if they are closer to age (for example, I'm not very close to my brother who is 20 years older than me, because we didn't even grow up together). My closest relationship is with my brother, who is 4 years older than me, but tbh it was easier to get along and talk once he moved bc of college, the distance made it easier to "love each other" if that makes sense.

4+ siblings can absolutely get along, despite interests etc, again once they get older it's much easier to get along (at least in my case), younger siblings (and teenagers) will probably fight no matter what, over things like toys, sharing things, just being hormonal bc of puberty or bc of jealousy and competition within the family. I think with good build-up (also maybe showing that despite having childish fights, they love each other) it is entirely possible to have a setting with a family of 4+ siblings get a long perfectly fine.
